# command: go run ./cmd/realdata -file data/online_retail_II.xlsx
# go version: go1.26.5 darwin/arm64
# dataset: UCI Online Retail II, https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/502/online+retail+ii (download: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/502/online+retail+ii.zip)
# licence: CC BY 4.0. Only aggregate statistics and a few StockCode/description labels appear below.
# sha256 of the .xlsx: bcbe73b35f5b7babf197fb0cb983a11f5d9ff929078d4aa53d171b1f2df2e980
# no ground truth: real sales data has no known elasticity, so nothing below can show an estimate is right
#
# rules (fixed before any estimate was computed):
#   Each line is counted under the first rule that drops it, in this order:
#   R0  a line in sheet "Year 2010-2011" whose Invoice also appears in sheet "Year 2009-2010" is dropped:
#       the two sheets overlap on 2010-12-01..2010-12-09 and the second repeats lines of the first
#   R1  malformed: missing or unparseable Invoice, StockCode, Quantity, InvoiceDate or Price, or non-integer Quantity
#   R2  cancellation: Invoice starts with "C"
#   R3  Quantity <= 0
#   R4  Price <= 0, or Price that rounds to 0 pence
#   R5  non-product: StockCode (upper-cased, trimmed) does not start with a digit (POST, DOT, M, BANK CHARGES, ...)
#   A product is a StockCode, upper-cased and trimmed. Price in pence = round(Price*100).
#   Day = calendar date of InvoiceDate as recorded, no time-zone shift; Observation.Day = days since 2009-12-01.
#   A store-open day is a calendar day with at least one kept line for any product; closed days give no observation.
#   Per product, one observation per store-open day from its first to its last sale day:
#     units = sum of quantity that day; price = the price with the most units that day, ties to the lower price;
#     an open day without a sale is Units 0 at the most recent price; OnPromo false (the data has no promotion flag).
#   Estimator: pricing.DefaultFitOptions() as shipped (volume gate on), no pooling. Gate-off run: MinMeanUnitsPerDay = 0.
#   No unit cost is known, so no price is proposed and the enforcer is not run.
#   Customer ID and Country are not used in sections A-D.
# fit options: MinDays 45, MinDistinctPrices 3, MinLogPriceSD 0.02, MaxRelativeHalfWidth 0.6, MinMeanUnitsPerDay 45,
#   ControlPromo true, WeeklySeasonality true, AnnualSeasonality true, Level 0.95

D. EVIDENCE ABOUT CONFOUNDING BY ORDER SIZE
   The dataset's description says many of this retailer's customers are wholesalers, and wholesale unit prices
   commonly fall with order size; (ii) tests that here. Where they do, a day's price and a day's units can both
   be driven by who ordered that day, and a negative slope can appear with no buyer responding to a price.

  (i) Product-days (a product on a day it sold) with more than one distinct unit price among its lines:
      100319 of 529744 product-days (18.9%), carrying 5064616 of 11221670 units (45.1%)
      Can show: how often one day's sales of one product happened at several prices, which the daily
      series collapses to the price with the most units. Cannot show: why the prices differed.

  (ii) Products with at least 200 kept lines: 1466. Split each product's lines at its lower-median line
      quantity m: large = quantity >= m, small = quantity < m; compare units-weighted mean unit prices.
      68 excluded because every line is >= m (no small group); 1398 compared.
      large lines priced strictly lower than small lines: 1382 of 1398 (98.9%)
      median of (large mean price / small mean price): 0.710
      Can show: whether bigger lines of the same product paid less per unit. Cannot show: that this
      moved the daily series, or by how much it biases any one estimate.

  (iii) The 63 products usable with the gate ON, re-estimated from only their lines with quantity <= m
      (retail-sized lines; same store-open days; range = first to last day with a retained line).
      gate ON (primary): 2 of 63 still usable; refused: too_few_days 1, too_few_distinct_prices 11, volume_too_low 49
        retail-only minus all-lines elasticity (n=2): 25% +0.082, median +0.330, 75% +0.578; less negative in 1 of 2
      gate OFF (secondary: cutting lines cuts volume, which the gate alone would refuse): 43 of 63 still usable; refused: too_few_days 1, too_few_distinct_prices 11, not_distinguishable_from_zero 2, interval_too_wide 6
        retail-only minus all-lines elasticity (n=43): 25% +0.539, median +0.855, 75% +1.376; less negative in 38 of 43
      Can show: how much an estimate moves when the largest lines are taken out. Cannot show: which of
      the two is nearer the truth; the retail-only series is thinner and has confounders of its own.
      Caution (added after review): keeping lines by quantity cuts off the high-unit lines, which by itself
      flattens daily units and pulls a slope toward zero. This shift is expected with or without confounding.

  (iv) Added after review, because (ii) pools two years and a price that rose while order sizes fell would
      look the same. Inside each product-day with more than one price: was the mean line quantity at that
      day's lowest price larger than at its highest price?
      lowest-price lines were larger: 84192 of 100319 product-days (83.9%); equal: 6810; smaller: 9317
      Can show: that on the same day, for the same product, the cheaper lines were the bigger ones, which
      time cannot explain. Cannot show: how much this moves any one estimate.

F. SECOND RUN WITH ONE RULE CORRECTED (cancelled orders netted out)
   Sections A-D are the primary result and stand as printed. This section repeats A-C with one rule added
   after the first run showed it was needed; section D is not recomputed.
   R2b (corrected rule, added after the first run): R2 drops a cancellation but keeps the order it reversed,
       so a reversed order still counted as a sale. Here, after R0-R5, each cancellation line (Invoice "C...",
       Quantity < 0, with a Customer ID, product StockCode), taken in time order, removes the latest still-unmatched
       kept line with the same Customer ID and StockCode and the opposite Quantity, dated at or before it.
       Price need not match. A cancellation with no match removes nothing. Everything else is as in sections A-C.
   cancellation lines eligible to match: 17641; matched and removed: 6255 kept lines, 406735 units
   kept lines now: 1008690; store-open days: 604; products: 4699

E. WHAT THIS SHOWS
   As shipped, the estimator answers for 63 of 4707 products (1.3%), which sold 19.5% of units; the volume gate alone refuses 2682 (57.0%).
   Without the gate it would answer for 2396 (50.9%), 94.1% below -1; 2333 of those sell under the 45-a-day floor that cmd/sweep set on synthetic data.
   Larger lines paid less per unit in 1382 of 1398 products with 200+ lines (median price ratio 0.71), and 45.1% of units sold on product-days with more than one price.
   So a day's price and a day's units can both move with who ordered that day, and the model has no control for it.
   Refitting the 63 usable products on retail-sized lines leaves 2 usable with the gate on; with it off, 38 of 43 move toward zero (median +0.86).
   These estimates are consistent with order-size confounding; this run cannot say how much of any estimate it explains, or that any estimate is right.
   Netting out cancelled orders (section F, a rule added after the first run) takes the gate-on usable count from 63 to 59.
